subject: physics_2
question_text: What are meant by equipotential surfaces?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: definition matches NCERT; the surface of a charged conductor is equipotential (the book's example); W = qΔV = 0 for movement on the surface, the standard added property.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: A surface that has the same electric potential
at every point on it is called an
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words same potential at every point are the definition.
steps.why: One value of V shared by every point of the surface is the whole content of the word equipotential — equal potential.
common_mistakes: Saying "same field at every point". The surface shares one POTENTIAL, not one field.

recall.must_convey: That an equipotential surface has the same potential at every point on it.
accept: one value of V over the surface

steps.memory_tip: Equi-potential: equal potential. The name is the definition.

steps.label: Example and property
lines: The surface of a charged conductor is an
equipotential surface. No work is done in
moving a charge on an equipotential surface,
because V does not change: W = qΔV = 0.

lines.text: Same V at every point of the surface

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Give the conductor-surface example; the zero-work line supports it.
steps.why: Work in an electric field is charge times the change in potential. On an equipotential surface the change is zero, so the work is zero — this is why the field must meet the surface at right angles.
common_mistakes: Giving no example. The charged conductor's surface is the expected one.
Writing W = qV instead of W = qΔV. Work uses the CHANGE in potential.

recall.must_convey: That a charged conductor's surface is an example, and no work is done moving a charge on such a surface.
accept: no work moving a charge on it
W equals q delta V equals zero

steps.memory_tip: Conductor surface for the example; no change in V, so no work.

insider_note: The definition alone is one mark; the conductor-surface example is what completes the two.
